newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cocoa physicals just ticking over in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa physicals just ticking over in Germany.

text.p: Cocoa bean and butter trades in Germany remained sluggish in lack of origin supply news and as sterling rose sharply versus the mark, traders said on Wednesday.
"Turnover is extremely thin apart from some spot business," one said.
"We're used to the Ivory Coast crop range at 850,000-950,000 tonnes and sterling has moved from 2.30 marks to nearly 2.38 marks over the last four weeks."
These factors overruled encouraging news today the third quarter German bean grind was seven percent higher than last year's third quarter figure at 65,824 tonnes.
Traders, who cited a cool summer and export activity, said this fitted in with generally positive demand news in Europe.
"There is no doubt that actual consumption has risen because the wholesale trade keeps low chocolate stocks and storage facilities in eastern Europe are limited," one said.
But processors were well covered and futures were looking to the supply side for direction, the traders said.
"I believe the market wants to go higher...traders want to re-establish contact with origin but there would have to be a crop-related reason," one said.
Local bean prices were little changed from last month at 2.28-2.35 marks/kg for fourth quarter 1996 and 2.35 marks for first quarter 1997.

The 1996 cocoa butter ratio remained at 2.83-2.84 for 1996 dates with implied cocoa butter prices liquid ex-works at 6.50-6.56 marks. The first quarter 1997 ratio was 2.73-2.74 and the mark price 6.50-6.51.
London Dec futures were up two stg from last night at 976 at 1530 GMT and sterling fixed today at 2.387 marks in Frankfurt. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
